title: Seasonal review annotated scratchpad
summary: Working notes for my seasonal performance touchpoint. Informal; meant to capture stories, data points, and questions to bring to a 1:1. Focus: impact highlights, gaps to address, career asks, and concrete evidence to back recommendations.
content:
Purpose:
- Quick, portable capture for the upcoming seasonal review with manager (week of Mar 15).
- Use as a prompt list during 1:1 + as a skeleton for the formal self-review doc later.

Style notes (to self):
- Keep stories short (3-4 lines), include metric or artifact when possible.
- Tag each item as: (impact), (risk), (ask).
- Be explicit about time requested or support needed (e.g., 1:1 to discuss, manager intro, budget).

Impact highlights (short stories):
1) Hiring pipeline stabilization (impact)
- Ran two-week experiment changing recruiter outreach template + standardized rubric for first-screen.
- Result: interview-to-offer ratio improved (qualitative: fewer low-fit screens; data: ~12% lift in qualified interview rate in Feb sample).
- Artifact: Slack thread + recruiter rubric doc (linked in Confluence).

2) Onboarding sprint: triage -> action (impact)
- Led cross-team sprint to cut new-hire ramp friction: clarified first-week tasks, created checklist, and 2 short walkthrough videos.
- Anecdote: two new hires said checklist reduced confusion in week 1.
- Metric: target new-hire time-to-first-meaningful-contribution down by estimated 1 week (need to quantify with SRE onboarding data).
- Artifact: onboarding checklist draft (Linear PO-129).

3) Calibration prep & compensation context (risk -> ask)
- Ran compensation benchmarking for IC2/IC3 ranges; found midband compression vs market.
- Risk: retention pressure for a specific node (SRE generalist).
- Ask: one-time calibration discussion and potential spot adjust recommendation for April comp cycle.

Gaps and experiment failures (important to bring up):
- Candidate texting pilot: high initial response but increased coordinator load; net time-to-offer not better.
- Action: propose automating scheduling follow-ups with Calendly flow + templated messages.

Evidence snippets (links + one-line context):
- recruiter-rubric-v2.md -> shows rubric changes and scores used in Feb batch.
- onboarding-checklist-v1.xlsx -> checklist and tasks; used in Feb cohort.
- comp-benchmarks-Q1.pdf -> external market data and internal band analysis.

Manager prep questions (to ask in review):
- Which of these initiatives would you like me to prioritize next quarter? (hiring pipeline vs onboarding vs comp projects)
- Would you support a small headcount request (0.5 FTE recruiter capacity or contract) to sustain outreach volume?
- Can we schedule 30 minutes pre-calibration for me to share full comp pack and suggested language for manager meetings?
- What horizon do you see for moving into an individual contributor lead role vs manager-of-people role for me? (I want clarity so I can align goals.)

Signals & metrics I should surface (short list):
- time-to-offer median (Feb vs Dec baseline)
- interview-to-offer conversion (Feb batch sample)
- new-hire ramp proxy (task completion in weeks 1-3)
- churn risk flags (2-3 names + rationale)

Concrete asks (phrased for manager):
- Ask A: 30 min calibration prep meeting in April; I will bring a one-pager and suggested adjustments.
- Ask B: endorsement to trial a recruiter contract (3 months). If approved, I will build acceptance goals and reporting cadence.
- Ask C: short mentorship intro to a senior people-ops leader for career pathing (30-45 min).

Draft sentences for the formal self-review (snippets):
- "This season I led two initiatives that reduced noise in our hiring funnel and created a repeatable onboarding checklist that shortens ramp time for early-stage hires."
- "I identified a compression risk in our comp bands and prepared materials for calibration; I recommend a targeted spot-adjust for a critical role."

Open items to resolve before the 1:1:
- Pull exact time-to-offer numbers from recruiting data team (Chris).
- Convert anecdotal ramp feedback into 2-3 measurable checkpoints (ask Eng onboarding owner).
- Draft comp adjustment justification slides and send to manager 48 hours before calibration meeting.

Next steps (quick):
- [ ] Ask Chris for recruiting exports (deadline Mar 10).
- [ ] Draft 1-pager for comp adjustment (Mar 12).
- [ ] Schedule manager prep meeting (Mar 14).
- [ ] Convert checklist into README and link in new-hire welcome packet (Mar 20).

Random prompts to keep in the doc (notes-to-self):
- If manager asks about bandwidth: propose 20% time allocation for recruiting projects for next quarter and show ROI hypothesis.
- Keep one wins list: two concrete examples + customers (hiring managers) who gave positive feedback.
- Practice the 60-second pitch of each initiative before the review.

Tone/closing:
- This is messy by design. Move a subset into the formal self-review later this week.
- Use evidence over anecdotes where possible; but keep 1-2 human stories to illustrate impact.
quick_bullets: Be ready to reprioritize based on manager guidance
manager_questions: Which of these is highest priority for you next quarter?
Would you support a short-term contract recruiter to keep volume steady?
goals_summary: Short-term: stabilize hiring funnel and codify onboarding so ramp is predictable. Mid-term: contribute to calibration and compensation fairness. Career: grow ownership of cross-functional ops projects and move toward a lead IC role with occasional people-management responsibilities.
